events.credibility_reason: Known only through secondary reports (QbitAI, Nechita, Epoch); no primary post, technical report or decoder was obtained, the only reported check (VibeMathed) is second-hand and unidentified, and the list of further orders is inconsistent across sources.

events.ai_basis: we have reformulated the Hadamard maximal determinant problem in orders n≡3 (mod 4) as a reinforcement learning based sequence reconstruction problem
ai_systems_credited: reinforcement-learning policy (authors' own; GNN and autoregressive transformer decoder trained with PPO and GRPO fine-tuning; no named model)

why: The statement asks for md(n) for every n, so settling one order (15, 19, 37, 22, 428, 668) is a case and new record determinants are bounds. The order-668 event is a case: for 4 | n a Hadamard matrix attains n^(n/2), so if it is valid it fixes md(668). I marked it checkable because the record describes an explicit matrix that a short HH^T = 668I script would verify. I marked it doubtful because it reaches us only through secondary sources. Its AI role was the close call. The authors' only words are 'of course claude:))'. Epoch credits 'a team of three humans and Claude' as the solvers. Read together, these support Claude producing part of the construction, but they do not show that Claude produced it with humans only checking, so I chose assisted over generated or none. Butbaia et al. raises lower bounds at n = 51 and 103–119, so it is a bound, checkable through its CSV and verify script. By the authors' own appendix, their learning policies produced the records at 103, 111 and 115, so it is assisted. The methods are the authors' own neural RL policies, not a named model. Eliahou's mod-64 matrix and the complex and roots-of-unity papers are variants. The benchmarks, the failed AI attempts and the transformer paper at already-settled orders are none.
doubts: The 668 AI role depends on a thin quote plus third-party labelling. A technical report could move it to generated, or to none. Whether a custom RL policy (GNN/transformer trained with PPO) counts as an 'AI system' for the project is a definitional question; I treated it as one. The Butbaia quotes come from a summarising fetch. The record does not establish journal acceptance for Orrick 2004 or Brent et al. 2011, so those stay unreviewed. Orrick–Solomon was published in Discrete Math. (2007) per OEIS.
